intro: BBC Sport has put together a roundup of some of the best new kits released by clubs around the world over the summer and is inviting readers to vote for their top 10. The collection highlights the variety of designs that arrive ahead of each campaign, from home and away shirts to third strips and special editions.

sections.heading: Why kit launches are more than just a new shirt
sections.text:
A kit reveal is a major moment in the football calendar. For supporters it’s a visual statement of identity and pride; for clubs and manufacturers it’s a high-profile commercial opportunity. New shirts are often timed to coincide with the close of one season and the start of preparations for the next, which is why many releases appear over the summer.

Beyond aesthetics, modern kits can reflect broader themes — celebrating anniversaries, referencing historic colours, or incorporating design cues tied to a club’s locality. They come in multiple variants: the traditional home shirt, an away alternative, and often a third or special edition used for cup ties, continental fixtures or charity initiatives. Replica shirts sold to fans are a key revenue stream for clubs, while players typically wear performance versions that include advanced materials and fit adjustments.

sections.heading: How to choose your favourite new kits
sections.text:
When judging a kit, fans typically weigh several factors. Visual appeal and how well the design aligns with a club’s history matter a lot: subtle nods to previous eras can win over long-term supporters, while bolder, contemporary graphics may attract newer audiences. Quality of manufacturing, the reputation of the kit supplier, and how the shirt looks both on-pitch and as a replica for fans are practical considerations.

Sustainability and limited-edition releases have become part of the conversation too. Many clubs and brands now emphasise recycled fabrics or eco-conscious production methods, which can influence a supporter’s preference. Availability, price point and any attached fundraising or community elements also shape how memorable a kit becomes.

References to history, badge placement, meaningful details
Comfort, technology used, player vs replica differences
Use of recycled fabrics, transparent supply chains

analysis: There are a few recurring themes to watch when new kits are released. Retro references frequently resurface as clubs seek to tap into nostalgia, while manufacturers balance that with contemporary silhouettes and technical fabrics. Observers might also notice a rise in eco-friendly claims as sustainability becomes a selling point in the sports apparel market. Ultimately, how fans respond to a new shirt depends on a mix of tradition, fashion and the story the club and brand craft around the release.

faq.question: What did BBC Sport do in its roundup?
faq.answer: BBC Sport collected a selection of notable new kits that clubs around the world released over the summer and is asking readers to vote for their top 10 favourites.

faq.question: Can I vote for my favourite kits?
faq.answer: Yes. The BBC Sport feature invites readers to cast votes for their top 10 new kits from the roundup.

faq.question: When do clubs usually release new kits?
faq.answer: Clubs commonly unveil new kits in the off-season, often across the summer months, ahead of the coming campaign. Releases may coincide with pre-season preparations, anniversaries or promotional schedules agreed with kit suppliers.

conclusion: If you’ve enjoyed browsing the season’s new shirts, head to the BBC Sport roundup to see the full selection and submit your top 10. Voting is a simple way for fans to have their say on which designs have captured the imagination ahead of the new campaign.
